subject: Session capture retainability & proof-of-deletion request — Northbridge.ai
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@northbridge.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Northbridge Legal <legal@northbridge.ai>
Date: 2027-03-10T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify what gets stored for interactive sessions / proof-of-deletion request

Hi Logan,

We are preparing our security questionnaire and need some precise answers about Redwood's default behavior for hosted sessions. Our legal team specifically asked for: 1) which elements are stored by default for an interactive chat session (user input, model prompts, intermediate streamed fragments, final generated output, KV cache snapshots), 2) whether attachments uploaded during an interactive call (file uploads via the SDK) are retained, and 3) the mechanism and timeline for producing proof-of-deletion for a given user session (we may need a certificate or log showing tokens removed).

We'd appreciate a concise summary we can include in our vendor evaluation. I attached a simple diagram of our expected data flow. If this requires a short call, we can schedule.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Head of Platform Security
Northbridge.ai
Attachment: customer-data-flow.png
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@northbridge.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-10T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what gets stored for interactive sessions / proof-of-deletion request

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear note and diagram. Short answer up front: by default we retain (a) the raw request (user input + metadata), (b) the final model output, and (c) runtime traces needed for debugging (sampling/latency metrics). We do not persist transient streaming fragments as separate artifacts unless they are explicitly materialized by the client or exported to storage.

A few clarifications:
- Prompts vs. outputs: the full user prompt payload is stored as the request record; model-generated completions are stored as the response artifact.
- Streaming fragments: our streaming layer buffers fragments in-memory for delivery; fragments are not written to long-term logs unless your integration calls the "persist_session" API or saves transcripts.
- KV cache / internal runtime artifacts: these are ephemeral and flushed on session termination; they are not persisted to customer-visible storage by default.
- Attachments: file uploads are treated as objects in the customer's chosen storage configuration. If you upload via the hosted SDK and do not opt-in to external object storage, short-lived attachments are kept for the session processing window (default 24–48 hours) and then deleted unless you explicitly requested archival.

Proof-of-deletion: we can provide an audit record and deletion timestamp for the session ID. For enterprise contracts we also produce a signed deletion certificate (PDF) showing the session ID, retention policy applied, deletion job run id, and S3 purge evidence where applicable.

Looping in Kim and Marissa to add runbook specifics and the exact API calls you can use to trigger immediate erasure.

—Logan
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@northbridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-11T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what gets stored for interactive sessions / proof-of-deletion request

Thanks, Logan. Adding precise operational details for the questionnaire (feel free to copy):

1) Stored by default (hosted API):
   - request_record: user input text, request metadata (timestamp, model, client_id) — retained for the default retention horizon (45 days for hosted free tier; enterprise customers can set custom TTLs).
   - response_artifact: final model output (text, structured outputs) — retained same as request_record.
   - telemetry: token-level cost metrics, latency traces — retained in aggregate and raw form for 90 days for debugging; long-term analytics are aggregated.

2) Not persisted by default:
   - streaming fragments: buffered in-memory during active stream; not written to persistent logs unless the client writes a transcript to storage.
   - KV cache and internal runtime snapshots: ephemeral, not exposed or stored outside runtime nodes.

3) Attachments:
   - SDK upload: attachments are uploaded to our staging object store for model processing and removed after processing; default staging TTL is 48 hours.
   - If you configure Redwood to forward attachments to your own S3/GS bucket (recommended for retention control), we do not keep a copy beyond the processing window.

4) Deletion / proof-of-deletion:
   - Self-service: use the DELETE /v1/sessions/{session_id} API — returns a job id.
   - Proof artifacts: the job id links to a server-side purge job; we can export a signed certificate (PDF) and the purge run log showing S3 delete markers + timestamps. Standard export is available for enterprise customers; for SOC2 audits we include the certificate in the evidence bundle.

5) Edge cases:
   - If your integration uses transcript_export or streaming-to-destination features, those destinations control retention.
   - For EU residency: if you provision the account in eu region, data stays in-region by default and deletion jobs operate against eu buckets.

Laura — happy to provide a short paragraph your legal team can paste into the questionnaire.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Product Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@northbridge.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-11T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what gets stored for interactive sessions / proof-of-deletion request

Laura — attaching a short checklist and the runbook steps (see attached compliance-evidence-checklist.pdf) you can use when you need deletion evidence:

Runbook (summary):
- Step 1: Identify session_id(s) or customer identifiers.
- Step 2: Submit a deletion job via DELETE /v1/sessions/{session_id} (or open a support ticket if you need bulk purge).
- Step 3: Job processes and emits a purge_job_id; environmental region and bucket are recorded.
- Step 4: Once purge completes, the system generates a signed Deletion Certificate (PDF) and an associated purge log (sha256 checksums of deleted object names + timestamps).

Timeline expectations:
- Immediate API request acknowledgement: minutes.
- Backend purge across all material stores: typically completes within 24 hours for single-session deletes; bulk purges may take up to 72 hours depending on the dataset size and replication windows.

What we need from you to produce a certificate: session_id(s), customer tenant id, and preferred point of contact for signature.

Notes on evidence confidence: our deletion certificate includes the purge job id, bucket/object prefixes, and a signed timestamp. For customers that require additional assurance, we offer an on-demand attestation call with our infra team (DPA add-on).

Attachment: compliance-evidence-checklist.pdf

—Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

2) We'll start with a single-session purge as a test; I'll send the session_id and tenant id to support@redwood.ai unless you prefer we open a ticket in the portal.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Laura
